subject: Quest helper arrow and quest-log grouping
claim: The repository does not yet establish how the client selects an active quest helper arrow or groups goals in the quest log; roadmap fields such as destination zone, location, no-helper, and auto-selection are implementation hypotheses rather than verified client behavior.
how_to_repeat: Use a disposable account and an Ambrose server bound only to loopback with two authored quests: one with a single waypoint goal and one with two active goals pointing to different zones.
Accept the single-goal quest, then record the private client-visible helper destination, quest-log grouping, map marker presence, and the metadata of the quest messages that supplied them.
Accept the two-goal quest and vary goal order, goal completion state, NoQuestHelper, and skip-helper-auto-selection settings one case at a time.

Complete the first goal while the second remains active, then record only the selected helper target, goal ordering, progress counts, destination-zone identifiers, message names, directions, frame ordering, and payload lengths.
Repeat after relogging and after changing zones to distinguish persisted grouping from transient helper selection; keep captures, client files, credentials, payloads, and display text private.
evidence: The contributor-track lists F-05 as an open quest finding for helper-arrow selection and quest-log grouping.

The phase 7 roadmap names GoalLocation, GoalDestinationZone, NoQuestHelper, SkipQuestHelperAutoSelect, and MSG_SENDGOAL fields, but does not prove their client-visible precedence or grouping behavior.
The phase 10 roadmap separately calls for helper progress, map markers, hidden quests, and next-world behavior, with the real-client checks still unverified.
No quest-helper or quest-log grouping finding currently exists under contrib/findings/quests.
disproof: A repeatable multi-goal client trace establishes helper precedence, grouping, persistence, and flag behavior across the listed cases; that evidence should replace this gap record rather than be treated as confirmation of it.
